claims.text: The local catalog places Expansion Sheet Series 2 Red on June 17, 1998.
The local release models 36 unique catalog rows for Series 2 Red.
The local release identifies the product as glossy Vending/Expansion Sheet cards, with Pokellector as source and Bulbapedia caption metadata used for artist-credit texture.

The pre-English symbol-status matrix marks Expansion Sheet Series 2 Red as prints_without_rarity_symbol: no, high confidence, with trap consequence that vending cards are glossy and not the Base No Rarity lane.

The release has a common-rarity surface but contains high-memory rows including Moltres, Articuno, Zapdos, Lapras, Raichu, Ditto, Aerodactyl, and Master Ball; common rarity is therefore not a proxy for low collector meaning.

The local sheet carries a wide illustrator roster including Atsuko Nishida, Mitsuhiro Arita, Tomokazu Komiya, Sumiyoshi Kizuki, Naoyo Kimura, Nobuyuki Habu, Miki Tanaka, Shin-ichi Yoshida, Kagemaru Himeno, Keiji Kinebuchi, and Hikaru Koike.

Series 2 Red matters because it puts legendary Pokemon, odd creature art, and Trainer objects into a glossy vending-sheet body. The distribution form is identity: these are not booster memories wearing a different name.
Agents should preserve Japanese title, date, row number, glossy vending-sheet format, Common rarity signal, artist-credit source, and no/not-Base-No-Rarity symbol boundary before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Expansion Sheet Series 2 Red — legendary memory from a vending machine
narrative.why_it_matters: Series 2 Red is a little dazzling because it refuses to rank memory the normal way. The local rarity signal says Common all the way down, and then the sheet hands you Moltres, Articuno, Zapdos, Lapras, Raichu, Ditto, Aerodactyl, Master Ball. The chase is not only rarity; it is the assembly: glossy vending stock, row discipline, machine distribution, and a wide early illustrator bench. This is exactly why the catalog needs to speak in routes and surfaces instead of flattening everything into a price list.
